open.what: Pylon's harbour at dusk. A loop of track runs round the dock: a cart takes on a crate of sentences, goes through the scoring shed, past the crane, and back. Pylon checks her clipboard. No words.

segments.heading: The training loop
lines: The training loop. Five steps, two thousand times.
Every lesson so far has a piece of training in it. Tonight they go round together, and we watch the whole loop teach the attention model, from the first step to the last.

segments.heading: One lap
lines: One lap goes like this. Take a batch of {{recipe.model.batch}} rows from the training text. Run the model forward and score every next word: that is the loss.
Run backward to get the slope for every one of the model's {{recipe.model.nParams|int}} numbers. Then the optimiser takes one step downhill. That is one lap.

On one core of our test machine, with this lesson's own code, a lap takes about {{speed.msPerStep|int}} milliseconds, and most of that is the backward pass: {{speed.anatomy.backwardOnly|int}} of them.

segments.heading: The settings
lines: The optimiser is Adam, with a little weight decay that shrinks most of the numbers slightly each step, as in AdamW. The layer norms' gains and the biases are left out.
The step size starts tiny and grows over the first {{recipe.defaults.warmup}} laps to {{recipe.defaults.lr}}. That is warmup.

And if the whole slope, all the numbers taken together, is ever longer than {{recipe.defaults.clip}}, it is shortened to {{recipe.defaults.clip}} before the step. That is clipping. It fired on {{gradients.stats.clipped}} of the {{gradients.stats.n|int}} laps, {{gradients.byWindow.0.clipped}} of them in the first {{gradients.byWindow.0.to}}.

segments.heading: Two thousand laps
lines: Now run it. At lap zero, the held-out loss is {{reproduce.milestones.0.heldOut|f2}}, a blind guess.
By lap {{reproduce.milestones.1.step}} it is {{reproduce.milestones.1.heldOut|f2}}: the easy patterns, which word tends to follow which, come first.

Copying a word from far back comes late, and then fast. At lap {{reproduce.milestones.2.step}}, copying is right {{reproduce.milestones.2.copyAccuracy|pct}} percent of the time. By lap {{reproduce.milestones.3.step}}, {{reproduce.milestones.3.copyAccuracy|pct}} percent.
We ran the loop again from the same seeds, and got the attention lesson's model back exactly: {{reproduce.tensorsEqual}} of {{reproduce.tensorsTotal}} weight tables, number for number.

predict.question: Will copying a word from far back be learned early, late, or bit by bit?

segments.heading: Change one thing
lines: Change one setting at a time, train for {{variants.reference.steps|int}} laps, and compare. First, the noise: the same recipe on two other sets of training rows ends at {{variants.noise.0.summary.heldOut|f2}} and {{variants.noise.1.summary.heldOut|f2}}, and the original at {{variants.reference.summary.heldOut|f2}}, all three within a few thousandths. A difference smaller than that cannot be told apart from luck.

A step size ten times smaller ends at {{variants.runs.0.summary.heldOut|f2}}, and copies right only {{variants.runs.0.summary.copyAccuracy|pct}} percent of the time. Ten times larger ends worse, at {{variants.runs.2.summary.heldOut|f2}}, copying {{variants.runs.2.summary.copyAccuracy|pct}} percent.
Without weight decay: {{variants.runs.4.summary.heldOut|f2}}, inside the noise. On this small model, at this length, it makes no difference we can see.

Batches of 4 rows for the same number of laps see a quarter of the text, and end at {{variants.runs.5.summary.heldOut|f2}}. Given the same text over four times the laps, they still end at {{variants.runs.6.summary.heldOut|f2}}.

predict.question: Make the step size ten times larger. Faster, or worse?

segments.heading: A loop that cannot learn
lines: Two broken loops, as checks. With a step size of zero, nothing moves: the loss stays at {{controls.runs.0.summary.heldOut|f2}}.
Turn every slope around, so each step goes uphill, and the loss climbs to {{controls.runs.1.summary.heldOut|int}}. The loop only works because the slope points the right way.

segments.heading: Goodnight
lines: Batch, forward, loss, backward, step. Two thousand times, and a blind guess becomes a model that copies.
Next on the dock: what goes into the batches. Goodnight.
